blocks.prompt: 7 (i) Find the square root of the complex number \(-7 - 24i\).
blocks.explanation:
Humein woh do complex numbers chahiye jinka square \(-7 - 24i\) ho. Har non-zero complex number ke bilkul do square roots hote hain, aur dono ek doosre ke negative hote hain.
Diya kya hai? \(z = -7 - 24i\), yani \(x = -7\), \(y = -24\).
Rule kaunsa? Section 1.2.1 ka square root formula, jo \(|z|\), \(p\) aur \(q\) se kaam karta hai.
Plan: pehle \(|z|\), phir \(p\) aur \(q\), phir \(y\) ke sign se signs ka faisla, aur aakhir mein square kar ke check.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(z = -7 - 24i\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\sqrt{z}\), dono square roots.
Tareeqa: Square root ka formula (Section 1.2.1): \(p = \sqrt{\frac{|z| + x}{2}}\), \(q = \sqrt{\frac{|z| - x}{2}}\); agar \(y > 0\) ho to \(\sqrt{z} = \pm(p + iq)\), aur \(y < 0\) ho to \(\pm(p - iq)\). Yeh formula kisi bhi \(x + iy\) ke dono square roots seedha de deta hai, is liye har dafa \((a + ib)^2\) expand kar ke equations banane ki zaroorat nahi. Sirf teen cheezein chahiye: \(x\), \(y\) ka sign, aur \(|z|\).

\(x\) aur \(y\) parhein
\[x = -7,\quad y = -24 < 0\]
Kyun: Pehle number ko \(x + iy\) shakal mein dekh kar real part \(x\) aur imaginary part \(y\) pehchante hain. \(x\) formula mein jayega, aur \(y\) ka sign aakhir mein yeh tay karega ke jawab ke dono hisson ke signs ek jaise honge ya ulte. Is liye \(y\) ka sign abhi se note kar lein.

Modulus \(|z|\) nikalein
\[|z| = \sqrt{(-7)^2 + (-24)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{49 + 576}\]
\[= \sqrt{625} = 25\]
Kyun: Modulus \(|z| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) number ki origin se doori hai (jaise naqshe par ghar se school ka seedha faasla). Yeh \(p\) aur \(q\) dono ke formula mein chahiye, is liye pehle isay nikalte hain. Squares lene se minus khatam ho jata hai, is liye modulus hamesha positive hota hai.

\(p\) nikalein
\[p = \sqrt{\dfrac{25 + (-7)}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{9} = 3\]
Kyun: \(|z|\) aur \(x\) ko \(p = \sqrt{(|z| + x)/2}\) mein rakha. \(p\) jawab ka real part hai. \(25 - 7 = 18\), aur \(18/2 = 9\).
Dhyan dein: \(x\) negative hai, is liye \(|z| + x\) mein asal mein minus hota hai aur \(|z| - x\) mein plus. Bracket laga kar likhiye taake sign ki ghalti na ho.

\(q\) nikalein
\[q = \sqrt{\dfrac{25 - (-7)}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{16} = 4\]
Kyun: \(|z|\) aur \(x\) ko \(q = \sqrt{(|z| - x)/2}\) mein rakha. \(q\) jawab ke imaginary part ka size hai. \(25 - (-7) = 32\), aur \(32/2 = 16\).

Signs chunein
\[\sqrt{-7 - 24i} = \pm(3 - 4i)\]
Kyun: \(y\) negative hai, is liye formula ka \(\pm(p - iq)\) wala hissa lagta hai: real part aur \(i\) wale part ke signs ulte honge. Wajah: root ka square karne par imaginary part \(2pq\) wale sign se aata hai; ulte signs hon to woh negative banta hai, jaisa \(y\) hai.

Tasdeeq: root ka square karein
\[(3 - 4i)^2 = 9 - 24i + 16i^2\]
\[= -7 - 24i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(16i^2 = -16\), to \(9 - 16 = -7\) aur \(2(3)(-4i) = -24i\). Square karne par wapas asal number aa gaya, is liye root sahi hai. Doosra root bas is ka negative hai, aur \((-w)^2 = w^2\), is liye woh bhi khud hi sahi hai. Yeh tasdeeq exam mein ek line mein ho jati hai aur ghalti foran pakar leti hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(\sqrt{-7 - 24i} = \pm(3 - 4i)\), yani \(3 - 4i\) ya \(-3 + 4i\)
Dono mein se kisi ka bhi square karein, \(-7 - 24i\) hi aata hai.

blocks.prompt: 7 (ii) Find the square root of the complex number \(8 - 6i\).
blocks.explanation:
Humein woh do complex numbers chahiye jinka square \(8 - 6i\) ho.
Diya kya hai? \(z = 8 - 6i\), yani \(x = 8\), \(y = -6\).
Rule kaunsa? Wohi square root formula; is dafa \(x\) positive hai, to hisaab aur aasaan hai.
Plan: \(|z|\), phir \(p\) aur \(q\), \(y\) ke sign se signs, aur square kar ke check. Part (i) dekh kar pehle khud try kijiye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(z = 8 - 6i\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\sqrt{z}\), dono square roots.
Tareeqa: Square root ka formula (Section 1.2.1): \(p = \sqrt{\frac{|z| + x}{2}}\), \(q = \sqrt{\frac{|z| - x}{2}}\); agar \(y > 0\) ho to \(\sqrt{z} = \pm(p + iq)\), aur \(y < 0\) ho to \(\pm(p - iq)\). Yeh formula kisi bhi \(x + iy\) ke dono square roots seedha de deta hai, is liye har dafa \((a + ib)^2\) expand kar ke equations banane ki zaroorat nahi. Sirf teen cheezein chahiye: \(x\), \(y\) ka sign, aur \(|z|\).

\(x\) aur \(y\) parhein
\[x = 8,\quad y = -6 < 0\]
Kyun: Pehle number ko \(x + iy\) shakal mein dekh kar real part \(x\) aur imaginary part \(y\) pehchante hain. \(x\) formula mein jayega, aur \(y\) ka sign aakhir mein yeh tay karega ke jawab ke dono hisson ke signs ek jaise honge ya ulte. Is liye \(y\) ka sign abhi se note kar lein.

Modulus \(|z|\) nikalein
\[|z| = \sqrt{8^2 + (-6)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{64 + 36}\]
\[= \sqrt{100} = 10\]
Kyun: Modulus \(|z| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) number ki origin se doori hai (jaise naqshe par ghar se school ka seedha faasla). Yeh \(p\) aur \(q\) dono ke formula mein chahiye, is liye pehle isay nikalte hain. Squares lene se minus khatam ho jata hai, is liye modulus hamesha positive hota hai.

\(p\) nikalein
\[p = \sqrt{\dfrac{10 + 8}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{9} = 3\]
Kyun: \(|z|\) aur \(x\) ko \(p = \sqrt{(|z| + x)/2}\) mein rakha. \(p\) jawab ka real part hai.

\(q\) nikalein
\[q = \sqrt{\dfrac{10 - 8}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{1} = 1\]
Kyun: \(|z|\) aur \(x\) ko \(q = \sqrt{(|z| - x)/2}\) mein rakha. \(q\) jawab ke imaginary part ka size hai. \(q = 1\) ka matlab hai jawab mein \(i\) ke saath sirf 1 aayega.

Signs chunein
\[\sqrt{8 - 6i} = \pm(3 - i)\]
Kyun: \(y\) negative hai, is liye formula ka \(\pm(p - iq)\) wala hissa lagta hai: real part aur \(i\) wale part ke signs ulte honge. Wajah: root ka square karne par imaginary part \(2pq\) wale sign se aata hai; ulte signs hon to woh negative banta hai, jaisa \(y\) hai.

Tasdeeq: root ka square karein
\[(3 - i)^2 = 9 - 6i + i^2\]
\[= 8 - 6i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(i^2 = -1\), to \(9 - 1 = 8\) aur \(2(3)(-i) = -6i\). Square karne par wapas asal number aa gaya, is liye root sahi hai. Doosra root bas is ka negative hai, aur \((-w)^2 = w^2\), is liye woh bhi khud hi sahi hai. Yeh tasdeeq exam mein ek line mein ho jati hai aur ghalti foran pakar leti hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(\sqrt{8 - 6i} = \pm(3 - i)\), yani \(3 - i\) ya \(-3 + i\)
Yeh do points origin ke aamne saamne hain, kyunke ek doosre ka negative hai.

blocks.prompt: 7 (iii) Find the square root of the complex number \(-15 - 36i\).
blocks.explanation:
Humein woh do complex numbers chahiye jinka square \(-15 - 36i\) ho.
Diya kya hai? \(z = -15 - 36i\), yani \(x = -15\), \(y = -36\).
Rule kaunsa? Wohi square root formula. Is dafa \(p\) aur \(q\) poore numbers nahi aayenge, surds (root wale numbers) aayenge; ghabraiye nahi, tareeqa wahi hai.
Plan: \(|z|\), \(p\), \(q\), signs, aur square kar ke check. Is part mein kitab ki answer key ghalat hai, neeche dekhiye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(z = -15 - 36i\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\sqrt{z}\), dono square roots.
Tareeqa: Square root ka formula (Section 1.2.1): \(p = \sqrt{\frac{|z| + x}{2}}\), \(q = \sqrt{\frac{|z| - x}{2}}\); agar \(y > 0\) ho to \(\sqrt{z} = \pm(p + iq)\), aur \(y < 0\) ho to \(\pm(p - iq)\). Yeh formula kisi bhi \(x + iy\) ke dono square roots seedha de deta hai, is liye har dafa \((a + ib)^2\) expand kar ke equations banane ki zaroorat nahi. Sirf teen cheezein chahiye: \(x\), \(y\) ka sign, aur \(|z|\).

\(x\) aur \(y\) parhein
\[x = -15,\quad y = -36 < 0\]
Kyun: Pehle number ko \(x + iy\) shakal mein dekh kar real part \(x\) aur imaginary part \(y\) pehchante hain. \(x\) formula mein jayega, aur \(y\) ka sign aakhir mein yeh tay karega ke jawab ke dono hisson ke signs ek jaise honge ya ulte. Is liye \(y\) ka sign abhi se note kar lein.

Modulus \(|z|\) nikalein
\[|z| = \sqrt{(-15)^2 + (-36)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{225 + 1296}\]
\[= \sqrt{1521} = 39\]
Kyun: Modulus \(|z| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) number ki origin se doori hai (jaise naqshe par ghar se school ka seedha faasla). Yeh \(p\) aur \(q\) dono ke formula mein chahiye, is liye pehle isay nikalte hain. Squares lene se minus khatam ho jata hai, is liye modulus hamesha positive hota hai. \(39^2 = 1521\) hai.

\(p\) nikalein
\[p = \sqrt{\dfrac{39 + (-15)}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\]
Kyun: \(|z|\) aur \(x\) ko \(p = \sqrt{(|z| + x)/2}\) mein rakha. \(p\) jawab ka real part hai. \(39 - 15 = 24\), \(24/2 = 12\), aur \(\sqrt{12} = \sqrt{4 \times 3} = 2\sqrt{3}\).
Dhyan dein: \(x\) negative hai, is liye \(|z| + x\) mein asal mein minus hota hai aur \(|z| - x\) mein plus. Bracket laga kar likhiye taake sign ki ghalti na ho.

\(q\) nikalein
\[q = \sqrt{\dfrac{39 - (-15)}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}\]
Kyun: \(|z|\) aur \(x\) ko \(q = \sqrt{(|z| - x)/2}\) mein rakha. \(q\) jawab ke imaginary part ka size hai. \(39 + 15 = 54\), \(54/2 = 27\), aur \(\sqrt{27} = \sqrt{9 \times 3} = 3\sqrt{3}\).

Signs chunein
\[\sqrt{-15 - 36i} = \pm(2\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3}\,i)\]
Kyun: \(y\) negative hai, is liye formula ka \(\pm(p - iq)\) wala hissa lagta hai: real part aur \(i\) wale part ke signs ulte honge. Wajah: root ka square karne par imaginary part \(2pq\) wale sign se aata hai; ulte signs hon to woh negative banta hai, jaisa \(y\) hai. Yahan roots poore numbers nahi hain, lekin surd wala jawab bilkul durust hai; isay \(\pm\sqrt{3}(2 - 3i)\) bhi likh sakte hain.

Tasdeeq: root ka square karein
\[(2\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3}\,i)^2\]
\[= 12 - 36i + 27i^2\]
\[= -15 - 36i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \((2\sqrt{3})^2 = 12\), \(2(2\sqrt{3})(3\sqrt{3}) = 12 \times 3 = 36\), aur \((3\sqrt{3})^2 i^2 = -27\). \(12 - 27 = -15\). Square karne par wapas asal number aa gaya, is liye root sahi hai. Doosra root bas is ka negative hai, aur \((-w)^2 = w^2\), is liye woh bhi khud hi sahi hai. Yeh tasdeeq exam mein ek line mein ho jati hai aur ghalti foran pakar leti hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(\sqrt{-15 - 36i} = \pm(2\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3}\,i)\), yani \(\pm\sqrt{3}(2 - 3i)\)
Answer key ka \(3 - 6i\) ghalat hai; hamara jawab square kar ke check ho chuka hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein \(3 - 6i\) ya \(-3 + 6i\) likha hai, jo ghalat hai: \((3 - 6i)^2 = 9 - 36i - 36 = -27 - 36i\) banta hai, \(-15 - 36i\) nahi. Sahi square roots \(\pm(2\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3}\,i)\) hain.

blocks.prompt: 7 (iv) Find the square root of the complex number \(119 + 120i\).
blocks.explanation:
Humein woh do complex numbers chahiye jinka square \(119 + 120i\) ho.
Diya kya hai? \(z = 119 + 120i\), yani \(x = 119\), \(y = 120\); is dafa \(y\) positive hai.
Rule kaunsa? Wohi square root formula. Numbers bare lag rahe hain, lekin \(119^2 + 120^2\) ek perfect square nikalta hai, to hisaab saaf ho jayega.
Plan: \(|z|\), \(p\), \(q\), \(y\) positive hone ki wajah se ek jaise signs, aur square kar ke check.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(z = 119 + 120i\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\sqrt{z}\), dono square roots.
Tareeqa: Square root ka formula (Section 1.2.1): \(p = \sqrt{\frac{|z| + x}{2}}\), \(q = \sqrt{\frac{|z| - x}{2}}\); agar \(y > 0\) ho to \(\sqrt{z} = \pm(p + iq)\), aur \(y < 0\) ho to \(\pm(p - iq)\). Yeh formula kisi bhi \(x + iy\) ke dono square roots seedha de deta hai, is liye har dafa \((a + ib)^2\) expand kar ke equations banane ki zaroorat nahi. Sirf teen cheezein chahiye: \(x\), \(y\) ka sign, aur \(|z|\).

\(x\) aur \(y\) parhein
\[x = 119,\quad y = 120 > 0\]
Kyun: Pehle number ko \(x + iy\) shakal mein dekh kar real part \(x\) aur imaginary part \(y\) pehchante hain. \(x\) formula mein jayega, aur \(y\) ka sign aakhir mein yeh tay karega ke jawab ke dono hisson ke signs ek jaise honge ya ulte. Is liye \(y\) ka sign abhi se note kar lein.

Modulus \(|z|\) nikalein
\[|z| = \sqrt{119^2 + 120^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{14161 + 14400}\]
\[= \sqrt{28561} = 169\]
Kyun: Modulus \(|z| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) number ki origin se doori hai (jaise naqshe par ghar se school ka seedha faasla). Yeh \(p\) aur \(q\) dono ke formula mein chahiye, is liye pehle isay nikalte hain. Squares lene se minus khatam ho jata hai, is liye modulus hamesha positive hota hai. \(169 = 13^2\), aur \(169^2 = 28561\).

\(p\) nikalein
\[p = \sqrt{\dfrac{169 + 119}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{144} = 12\]
Kyun: \(|z|\) aur \(x\) ko \(p = \sqrt{(|z| + x)/2}\) mein rakha. \(p\) jawab ka real part hai. \(169 + 119 = 288\), \(288/2 = 144\).

\(q\) nikalein
\[q = \sqrt{\dfrac{169 - 119}{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{25} = 5\]
Kyun: \(|z|\) aur \(x\) ko \(q = \sqrt{(|z| - x)/2}\) mein rakha. \(q\) jawab ke imaginary part ka size hai. \(169 - 119 = 50\), \(50/2 = 25\).

Signs chunein
\[\sqrt{119 + 120i} = \pm(12 + 5i)\]
Kyun: \(y\) positive hai, is liye formula ka \(\pm(p + iq)\) wala hissa lagta hai: dono parts ka sign ek jaisa. Ek root \(12 + 5i\) aur doosra \(-12 - 5i\).
Dhyan dein: \(12 - 5i\) jawab nahi hai; us ka square \(119 - 120i\) banta hai.

Tasdeeq: root ka square karein
\[(12 + 5i)^2 = 144 + 120i + 25i^2\]
\[= 119 + 120i \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(25i^2 = -25\), to \(144 - 25 = 119\) aur \(2(12)(5i) = 120i\). Square karne par wapas asal number aa gaya, is liye root sahi hai. Doosra root bas is ka negative hai, aur \((-w)^2 = w^2\), is liye woh bhi khud hi sahi hai. Yeh tasdeeq exam mein ek line mein ho jati hai aur ghalti foran pakar leti hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(\sqrt{119 + 120i} = \pm(12 + 5i)\), yani \(12 + 5i\) ya \(-12 - 5i\)
Dono roots ka square \(119 + 120i\) hai.
